title: Evaluating LLM-Based Credit Rating Systems: A Pre-Registered Specification-Curve Analysis — reproducibility artifact
description: Reproducibility artifact for the manuscript "Evaluating LLM-Based Credit Rating Systems: A Pre-Registered Specification-Curve Analysis." A pre-registered specification-curve (multiverse) study of whether large-language-model credit ratings are stable when the underlying fundamentals are held fixed but the elicitation is varied. From a frozen corpus, the analysis evaluates 45 credit-health profiles across 32 specifications and three seeds (4,320 credit-rating elicitations), drawn from a pre-registered 90-item battery and a balanced grid of model version, temperature, prompt paraphrase, output format, few-shot exemplars and presentation over two providers, benchmarked to Altman Z''. The estimand is stability, not accuracy. Under a descriptive main-effects decomposition no controllable axis exceeds about 5% of rating variance and pure run-to-run seed variation accounts for about 8%; instability persists on the temperature-0-honored subgrid (single provider, temperature 0; rating-invariance permutation p = 0.0005). Cross-specification agreement stays low at every resolution (unweighted Fleiss' kappa at most 0.49 at the investment-grade/high-yield split, where 25.2% of matched pairs disagree), and switching or pooling providers does not remove it. Specification variation is also observed in 31 perturbed and fingerprint-screened real issuers benchmarked to disclosed agency ratings; a post-hoc flagship model-tier arm does not detect attenuation on larger models, and a post-hoc reasoning-architecture arm (DeepSeek-R1, native chain-of-thought) shows comparable instability. The artifact derives and validates a candidate operational, ground-truth-free specification-instability score (held-out ROC-AUC 0.94; 0.70 on the real-issuer arm), and reports honest limits: cross-model transfer of the score is moderate but inconsistent across model pairs (Spearman 0.14-0.73), and the fractional design has near-orthogonal main effects with bounded residual aliasing (main off-diagonal correlation 0.062; main x two-factor-interaction 0.333). A single offline entry point (reproduce.sh) regenerates every reported number, table and figure from the frozen inputs, deterministically (seed 42), with no network access, no API keys and no paid model calls; live model capture is retained for transparency only and is not part of the reproduction.
